drafts.title: Is training a local LLM on the 2018 International Building Code practical for targeted building code analysis?
drafts.body: I've come across a discussion where someone wants to train a local LLM specifically on the 2018 International Building Code (IBC) to answer queries about building code analysis, potentially using inputs like floor plans. The core question is whether limiting a model to just one detailed technical document can produce focused and accurate responses, especially compared to using cloud-based models like ChatGPT with carefully crafted prompts. Given that the source author is a layperson and hasn't provided concrete performance data, I'm curious about the feasibility of this approach. Has anyone here experimented with training or fine-tuning local LLMs on a single specialized document for domain-specific tasks? How do the results typically compare to cloud models, particularly when prompt engineering is factored in? Also, what challenges might arise in representing inputs like floor plans for such models? Any insights or experiences would be appreciated.

drafts.title: Can a local LLM focused solely on the 2018 International Building Code outperform cloud models for building code queries?
drafts.body: There's an archived post from mid-2025 discussing the idea of creating a local AI model trained exclusively on the 2018 International Building Code to provide building code analysis from inputs such as floor plans. The author wonders if this narrow focus can yield more accurate and relevant answers than cloud models like ChatGPT, or if a well-crafted prompt on such a cloud model might suffice. Since the original poster is not an expert in LLMs and no empirical results were shared, I'm interested in hearing the community's take on this. What are the practical considerations and limitations when training a local LLM on a single, complex document? Could the lack of broader context hinder performance? And how might prompt engineering on cloud models compare in effectiveness for this kind of specialized retrieval?
